canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/06. Validate BST.cpp

narrative.title: The Range-Pass Audit of the Sort Racks
narrative.scenario: A warehouse's sort racks claim the strict smaller-left, larger-right layout, but a recent retrofit may have wedged crates into the wrong aisles. The auditor walks each station carrying a permissible value window: entering a left aisle tightens the ceiling, entering a right aisle raises the floor. Any crate outside its inherited window fails the audit on the spot.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) — not guaranteed to be a BST.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the tree satisfies the BST property for every node, otherwise false. Duplicate values are not allowed.

testCases.explanation: Node 4 sits in the right wing of 5 but holds a smaller value — the window check rejects it.
Every node stays inside the window its ancestors carved out.

hintLevels: Level 1: Checking only each parent-child pair is a trap — a violation can hide two levels down.
Level 2: Thread (low, high) bounds through the recursion: left children inherit a tighter ceiling, right children a tighter floor.
Level 3: Use wide integer sentinels (or longs) so boundary values like 2^31-1 don't fall outside every window.
